chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab al-'Abid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'There was a slave girl for me, so she committed adultery. Shall I apply the Hadd penalty on her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but that should happen in secret, due to the state of the authorities.'

key_terms.أُحُدُّهَا: Shall I apply the Hadd penalty on her
key_terms.لِحَالِ السُّلْطَانِ: Due to the state of the authorities

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on applying the Hadd penalty for adultery to a female slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that while the Hadd penalty for adultery applies to slave girls, its execution is concealed rather than public, a ruling derived from the political discretion of the Sultan. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the visibility of legal penalties can be modulated by the ruling authority to suit the socio-political context, distinguishing it from the fixed public nature of penalties for free individuals.
